target.title: fix(agents): normalize surrogate cache fingerprints
target.body:
Closes #100957

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where prompt-cache/cache-trace fingerprinting could preserve malformed UTF-16 surrogate halves when serializing JSON-like diagnostic inputs, causing otherwise equivalent cache boundary payloads to hash differently when malformed external text is present.

## Why This Change Was Made

`stableStringify` now normalizes string values and object keys with the existing provider surrogate sanitizer through the lightweight `@openclaw/ai/internal/shared` barrel, so cache keys, cache trace digests, and diagnostics share the same malformed-surrogate behavior as provider outbound text without importing the default runtime barrel. The transport sanitizer reuses the same implementation while keeping its previous nullish-input guard.

## User Impact

Users and operators get more stable prompt-cache fingerprints when malformed Unicode reaches cache trace inputs. Valid surrogate pairs such as emoji are preserved, while unpaired high and low surrogate halves are removed before deterministic stringification.

## Evidence

Current head: `77bfe44eaf009555a13c5448e1c080f8bf954693`.

- Claim proved: malformed-surrogate values and object keys normalize to the same cache fingerprint as already-normalized input while valid emoji remain preserved.
  - Direct proof command: `node --import tsx --input-type=module` with a script importing `stableStringify` and hashing malformed-vs-normalized payloads.
  - Observed result: `serializedEqual: true`, `digestEqual: true`, `validPairPreserved: true`, digest `fe8b4c427f8736f1842ab5bd49741fdb4ecbd55360e184d1bb48ab2c42ddeb12` for both payloads.
- Claim proved: focused regressions still cover stable stringify and transport sanitizer behavior.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/stable-stringify.test.ts src/agents/transport-stream-shared.test.ts`
  - Result: passed 2 Vitest shards; `stable-stringify.test.ts` 5 tests passed, `transport-stream-shared.test.ts` 10 tests passed.
- Claim proved: the sanitizer resolves through the lightweight shared barrel instead of the runtime barrel.
  - Import smoke: `node --import tsx --input-type=module` importing `sanitizeSurrogates` from `@openclaw/ai/internal/shared`.
  - Result: `{"sanitized":"leftright"}`.
- Hygiene:
  - `git diff --check`
  - Result: passed.
- Related open PR search for `100957 surrogate cache` returned no open matches before this proof refresh.
